title: Personal Credit Cards: Rewards Card Closure Settlement
content:
This page of the Personal Credit Cards manual explains how the bank settles the closing of a rewards card within a single consultation.

## Scope

It governs the closing, at the cardholder's request, of an active rewards card on which a recently posted annual fee is still within its refund window, money is still owed and points remain unredeemed. The whole settlement is carried out synchronously in the one consultation, and no separate closure request is registered.

## Aim

Once settled, the card is closed, carries no unredeemed points, owes no more than what genuinely remains, and still has an automatic payment set to recover that remainder.

## Who acts

Correcting the annual fee is the one part the bank performs itself. Everything that commits the cardholder's money or points, or ends the account, is the cardholder's own act: the instruction that collects what remains, drawn on a PCB checking account of theirs that is active; the taking of the points as cash; and the confirmation that closes the card.

## How the parts bear on one another

- The collecting instruction is meant to recover no more than the cardholder genuinely owes on the closed card, and its figure is read from the card's ledger; an annual fee the charter does not let stand on a card closed inside the refund window is not owed.
- While money remains owed, the cash from the points goes to the account from which the remainder is to be collected, and the card's automatic payment instruction is what identifies that account.
- A confirmed closure extinguishes whatever points are still on the card.
- The option carried onto the closed card is the automatic payment instruction standing on the card when the confirmation takes effect.

## Timing

Nothing in the settlement is deferred. Each part takes effect the moment it is posted or recorded, the matter is finished within the one conversation, and every part draws only on what the records already hold, on what another part has just put on record, or on what the cardholder says during the conversation.
